title: orch add-on manifest v1 (orch-addon.toml, parsed)
description: See addon-manifest.md. Paths are relative to the folder that holds orch-addon.toml and must stay inside it (no '..', no absolute paths, no symlinks out).

orch_api.description: Version of the add-on contract (CLI, view, ext rules) this add-on was written for.

name.description: Command `orch <name>`, ext key ext.<name>, folder .orch/addons/<name>/, config table [<name>], skill folder orch-<name>, AGENTS markers orch:addon:<name>.

description.description: One plain sentence for `orch addon list` and `orch --help`.

run.description: Top-level Python module. `orch <name> <args>` runs `<orch's python> -m <run> <args>` as a subprocess (addon-manifest.md, CLI contract).

skill.description: Folder with SKILL.md (frontmatter name: orch-<name>). Copied to .agents/skills/orch-<name>/.

agents_block.description: Markdown body of the AGENTS.md block. Default: <skill>/AGENTS-block.md.

ticket_ext.description: Local JSON Schema (no remote $ref, max 32 KB) for ticket ext.<name>. Without it the add-on writes no ticket data.

background.description: true = the add-on has a long-running process. It must implement `orch <name> start|stop|status --json`; `orch start`/`orch stop` and deactivation call them (addon-manifest.md, Background).

label.description: Nav label, one or two words.

order.description: Position in the nav after the built-in tabs.

panel.description: Optional extra card the dashboard draws on this tab (a fixed set; the page code never matches add-on names).

dashboard.description: The add-on has a dashboard tab, filled by `orch <name> view --json` (addon-view.schema.json).

ticket_view.description: Rows in the ticket detail slot, from ext.<name>. A row whose value is missing/null/empty is hidden.

format.description: open-page = an 'Open' button to [page] path + '/' + the field value (needs [page]); shown only when the value is set.

recommended.description: true = `orch init --recommended` turns it on. The core lists no add-on by name.

gitignore.description: Lines added to the workspace .gitignore by `orch addon add` and removed by `orch addon remove`. Relative paths inside the workspace: no leading '/', no '..', no backslash, no drive letter.

runs_agents.description: true = the add-on starts agent runs (always through `orch run start`).

requires.description: Add-on names that must be active first. `orch addon add` refuses with the missing names; nothing is turned on by itself.

needs.description: true = the add-on has `orch <name> needs --json` (rows of needs.schema.json) for `orch needs`.

ticket_links.description: Reference types this add-on knows (ticket refs, workspace/src/orch/refs.py). While the add-on is on, `orch ref add` gives a matching address this kind, and its references show with label, icon and status; off, they show as known site or plain Reference. Kinds are unique; url, ticket, artifact and file are reserved.

icon.description: Icon name; the page shows the known site's tile when the address is a known site, else a tile with the label's first letters.

match.description: Address pattern; * = one part of the address (no / ? #), a * at the end also takes the rest.

preview.description: Artifacts tab and phone show the link's thumb picture.

ticket_fields.description: Fields under the ticket's Details, stored in ext.<name> and edited in place (`orch ticket set <id> <name>.<field> <value>`). Field types come from the schema: enum = choice, number/integer = number, format date = date, format uri = url, string = text; readOnly = filled in by the add-on; x-hidden = not shown.

schema.description: JSON Schema of ext.<name> (default and must equal ticket_ext when both are set).

show_on_card.description: Fields shown as a quiet chip on board cards.

acts.description: What `orch <name> act <verb> [--by X] --json -- <ticket>` offers. Core knows `refresh` (addon-manifest.md, Act: refresh).

path.description: Path on the add-on's own local page; the base url is the checked url of `orch <name> status --json` (http://127.0.0.1:<port>).

page.description: The add-on serves its own local page (needs background = true). The dashboard shows a button that opens it in a new tab.
